items.text: 黛玉冷笑道：「我就知道，別人不挑剩下的也不給我。」
items.answer: Daiyu sneered, "I knew it. No one would give me the leftovers."

errors.evidence: No one would give me the leftovers.
errors.why: The meaning is inverted: Daiyu complains she is given only what others left over, not that no one would give her leftovers.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: Feng Jie said, "I've been telling you all along that you're too weak; if the people at home keep treating you this way, how can we possibly manage?"

errors.evidence: if the people at home keep treating you this way
errors.why: 縱的家裡人這樣 means You-shi's indulgence has let the household servants behave like this; the candidate reverses it so the servants are treating her badly.

errors.evidence: how can we possibly manage?
errors.why: 還了得了 is a rhetorical 'this is intolerable / where will it end', not a question about managing.

errors.evidence: Feng Jie
errors.why: 鳳姐 is the familiar Xifeng, and 'Feng Jie' is an unnatural, partly literal rendering of the nickname.

items.text: 寶玉未及回言，只見舡頭上來了兩人，一僧一道，夾住寶玉說道：「俗緣已畢，還不快走。」
items.answer: Before Baoyu could reply, two figures—one a monk and the other a Taoist priest—appeared at the bow of the boat, flanking him as they said, "Your mortal ties are ended; why do you not hurry away?"

items.text: 平兒笑道：「『得饒人處且饒人』，得省的將就些事也罷了。
items.answer: Ping'er smiled and said, "Where it is possible to let people off, one should spare them; let's just make do with that."

errors.evidence: let's just make do with that
errors.why: Loses 'save trouble / let matters pass' and recasts general advice as a vague 'make do with that' proposal.

items.text: 黛玉道：「不曾讀，只上了一年學，些須認得幾個字。」
items.answer: Daiyu said, "I have never studied; I went to school for only one year and can barely recognize a few characters."

items.text: 因此劉姥姥看不過，乃勸道：「姑爺，你別嗔著我多嘴。
items.answer: For this reason, Liu Lao'ao could not bear to see it and advised him, saying, "Young master, do not be angry with me for speaking out of turn.

errors.evidence: Young master
errors.why: 姑爺 means son-in-law (Granny Liu addressing her daughter's husband), not 'young master'; the family relation is lost.

errors.evidence: Liu Lao'ao
errors.why: 劉姥姥 is mis-romanized (should be Granny Liu or Liu Laolao).

items.text: 李貴笑道：“不怕你老人家惱我，素日你老人家到底有些不正經，所以這些兄弟才不聽。
items.answer: Li Gui smiled and said, "I dare not offend you, my dear sir. You've always been a bit undisciplined, which is why these brothers don't listen to you."

errors.evidence: I dare not offend you, my dear sir.
errors.why: "不怕你老人家惱我" is a polite preface meaning "don't be angry if I speak frankly"; the candidate gives a different meaning that loses the apology for the frank criticism that follows.

errors.evidence: a bit undisciplined
errors.why: "不正經" means improper or undignified conduct, not lacking discipline.

errors.evidence: these brothers
errors.why: "兄弟" here means the younger schoolmates, and a literal "brothers" may mislead the reader.

items.text: 作者自云：因曾歷過一番夢幻之後，故將真事隱去，而借通靈之說，撰此《石頭記》一書也。
items.answer: The author says: Having once experienced a dream and an illusion, he has hidden the true events and, by means of the tale of the Spirit Stone, composed this book called The Story of the Stone.

errors.evidence: Having once experienced a dream and an illusion
errors.why: 夢幻 is a single notion, a dream-like illusion; splitting it into 'a dream and an illusion' is slightly off, though the meaning survives.

errors.evidence: he has hidden the true events
errors.why: The present perfect and the missing 'therefore' weaken the causal link 因…故; the experience motivating the concealment is blurred.

items.text: 孫悟空在傍聞講，喜得他抓耳撓腮，眉花眼笑，忍不住手之舞之，足之蹈之。
items.answer: Sun Wukong listened from the side, so delighted that he tweaked his ears and scratched his cheeks, with a smile in his eyes and joy in his heart; he could not help dancing with his hands and stomping with his feet.

errors.evidence: with a smile in his eyes and joy in his heart
errors.why: 眉花眼笑 (brows blooming, eyes smiling) is rendered loosely; the brows are lost and 'joy in his heart' is added, though the sense of beaming joy is kept.

errors.evidence: Sun Wukong listened from the side
errors.why: The word 'lecture' (講) is missing; it should say he listened to the lecture from the side.

items.text: 有一般天罡數，該三十六般變化；有一般地煞數，該七十二般變化。
items.answer: There is a class of Heavenly Stars destined for thirty-six transformations; there is a class of Earthly Fiends destined for seventy-two transformations.

errors.evidence: There is a class of Heavenly Stars destined for thirty-six transformations
errors.why: The source says there is a set of methods under the Heavenly Dipper number that comprises 36 transformations. The candidate instead has a class of stars 'destined for' them, which turns 數 into a class

errors.evidence: a class of Earthly Fiends destined for seventy-two transformations
errors.why: The word 數 (number) is dropped, so the numerological sense of 天罡數 and 地煞數 as number-sets of methods is lost.

items.text: 悟空道：「我自聞道之後，有七十二般地煞變化之功，觔斗雲有莫大的神通；善能隱身遯身，起法攝法。
items.answer: Wukong said, "Since I first heard the Way, I have mastered the power of seventy-two earth-shaking transformations and the tremendous spiritual ability of the Somersault Cloud; I am skilled in concealing my body and vanishing from sight, as well as invoking magical arts.

errors.evidence: seventy-two earth-shaking transformations
errors.why: 地煞 is the Disha (earthly) set of transformations, not 'earth-shaking'; this invents a meaning.

errors.evidence: as well as invoking magical arts.
errors.why: 起法攝法 is a pair (raise and draw in/control magic), but only invoking is rendered; 攝法 is missing.

errors.evidence: Since I first heard the Way
errors.why: 'first' is added and 'heard the Way' is rendered too literally, without the sense of studying under a master, though the Way is kept.

items.text: 卻說他師徒兩個策馬前來，直至山門首觀看，果然是一座寺院。
items.answer: Now they rode their horses forward with their master and disciple until they reached the mountain gate and looked on; indeed, it was a temple.

errors.evidence: they rode their horses forward with their master and disciple
errors.why: 他師徒兩個 means the two of them, master and disciple, are the travelers; the candidate makes a separate 'they' ride with a master and disciple, which garbles who is doing what.

errors.evidence: until they reached the mountain gate
errors.why: 山門 is the temple's main gate, not a gate to a mountain; the literal rendering may mislead.

items.text: 卻說那個妖王在洞裡歡喜道：「小的們，孫行者吃了虧去了。
items.answer: Now that demon king rejoiced in his cave: "My little ones, Sun Wukong has suffered a setback and gone."

items.text: 卻說三藏自貞觀十三年九月望前三日，蒙唐王與多官送出長安關外。
items.answer: Now, it was three days before the full moon in the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Zhenguan that Tripitaka, having been escorted out of Chang'an by Tang Wang and the officials, departed beyond the pass.

errors.evidence: Tang Wang
errors.why: "Tang Wang" leaves 王 untranslated and reads like a personal name; "the Tang king" is clearer.

errors.evidence: escorted out of Chang'an by Tang Wang and the officials, departed beyond the pass
errors.why: The phrasing is redundant and clumsy, and "departed beyond the pass" is awkward; "escorted out beyond the Chang'an pass" would be better.

errors.evidence: the officials
errors.why: "多官" (many officials) loses "many", and the honorific nuance of 蒙 is not conveyed.

items.text: 孔明囑付曰：「吾受劉皇叔三顧之恩，不容不出。
items.answer: Kongming said, "I have received the grace of Lord Liu's three visits and cannot refuse to go."

errors.evidence: Lord Liu's
errors.why: 劉皇叔 is 'Imperial Uncle Liu', a title tied to Liu Bei's kinship to the Han emperor; 'Lord Liu' loses that, though the person is still identifiable.

errors.evidence: Kongming said,
errors.why: 囑付 (instructed/charged his brother Zhuge Jun) is reduced to a plain 'said', so the addressee and the instructing sense are lost.

items.text: 玄德曰：「備乃中山靖王之後；自涿郡剿戮黃巾，大小三十餘戰，頗有微功，因得除今職。」
items.answer: Xuande said, "I am the descendant of Prince Jing of Zhongshan; since I led the slaughter of the Yellow Turbans in Zhuo, I have fought more than thirty battles of varying size and achieved some modest merit, thus earning my current post."

errors.evidence: since I led the slaughter of the Yellow Turbans
errors.why: The source does not say he "led" the campaign; this claim is added.

errors.evidence: in Zhuo,
errors.why: 涿郡 is rendered as "Zhuo" without "Commandery", and 自 is turned into a location rather than "from Zhuo Commandery". The loss is slight.

items.text: 玄德曰：「我與民秋毫無犯，那得財物與他？」
items.answer: Xuande said: "I have committed no offenses against the people and taken not a single scrap of their property; how could I give them wealth?"

errors.evidence: how could I give them wealth?
errors.why: 他 refers to the inspector (督郵), not the people; the sentence means 'where would I get money to give him as a bribe', so the recipient is wrong and the point about the bribe is lost.

errors.evidence: how could I give them wealth?
errors.why: 那得 means 'where would I get', i.e. he has nothing to give, but the candidate turns it into 'how could I give', which shifts the meaning.

items.text: 馬謖在山上見之，大笑曰：「彼若有命，不來圍山。」
items.answer: Ma Su saw them from the mountain and laughed aloud: "If they had any intention of attacking, they would not have come to besiege the mountain."

errors.evidence: If they had any intention of attacking, they would not have come to besiege the mountain.
errors.why: 有命 means 'if he values his life / has a destiny to live', not 'intention of attacking'; the mocking point that the enemy would not dare to besiege is lost, and the sentence is incoherent.

errors.evidence: they would not have come to besiege the mountain
errors.why: The source is a present-future conditional ('would not come to surround'), but the candidate uses a past counterfactual 'would not have come' and treats the siege as already happening.

errors.evidence: saw them
errors.why: 之 refers to Sima Yi, who scouted with about a hundred riders; 'them' is a defensible plural, but the focus on the enemy commander is lost.

items.text: 張飛性起，向玄德換了坐下馬，搶出陣來，叫曰：「我捉你不得，誓不上關！」
items.answer: Zhang Fei, his temper flaring, swapped seats with Xuande's horse and charged out of the formation, shouting: "If I cannot catch you, I swear never to enter the pass!"

errors.evidence: swapped seats with Xuande's horse
errors.why: 坐下馬 means the horse he rode; he exchanged mounts with Xuande, not 'seats with a horse', which is garbled.

items.text: 行到赤岸坡，見蜀兵已去遠，乃引還，顧謂眾將曰：「孔明已死，我等皆高枕無憂矣！」
items.answer: They reached the Red Bank Slope and saw that the Shu troops had already moved far away. They then turned back, and one of them looked at the generals and said, "Kongming is dead; we can all rest easy now!"

errors.evidence: one of them looked at the generals and said
errors.why: The speaker is Sima Yi, who turned to address his generals; the candidate makes an unnamed member of the group speak to the generals.

errors.evidence: They then turned back
errors.why: The source says Sima Yi led his troops back (引還), and the candidate drops the subject and the causal sense of leading the army.

items.text: 武松道：「只好恁地，卻又來望哥哥。」
items.answer: Wu Song said, "That will do; I'll come to see my brother again."

items.text: 智深尋思道：「這個大寺，如何敗落的恁地？」
items.answer: Zhishen pondered, "How has this great temple fallen into such ruin?"

items.text: 魯達道：「恁地時，洒家自去便了。」
items.answer: Lu Da said, "If that's the case, I'll just go on my own."

items.text: 宋江道：「兄弟，卻是你殺了小衙內，雖是軍師嚴令，論齒序他也是你哥哥，且看我面，與他伏個禮，我卻自拜你便了。」
items.answer: Song Jiang said, "Brother, you have indeed killed the young master. Although it was Master's strict order, by age he is your elder brother; please show him respect on my account, and I will bow to you myself."

errors.evidence: it was Master's strict order
errors.why: 軍師 means the strategist (Wu Yong); "Master" is an inaccurate, unclear rendering of the title.

errors.evidence: please show him respect on my account
errors.why: 伏個禮 means to make a bow of apology; "show respect" is vaguer and loses the bow.

errors.evidence: and I will bow to you myself.
errors.why: The sentence-final 便了 ("that will settle it") is dropped, so the offer reads as a bare statement rather than a settlement.

items.text: 酒家道：「客官，你須見我門前招旗上面明明寫道：『三碗不過岡』。」
items.answer: The innkeeper said, "Guest, you must see the banner clearly written above my door: 'Three bowls and one cannot pass the ridge.'"

errors.evidence: you must see the banner clearly written above my door
errors.why: 須見 means 'surely you must have seen' (a mild reproach), but 'must see' reads as an instruction or obligation and is awkward.

items.text: 戴宗連忙回轉身來問道：「壯士素不曾拜識，如何呼喚賤名？」
items.answer: Dai Zong immediately turned around and asked, "Sir, I have never had the honor of meeting you. How do you know my humble name?"

errors.evidence: How do you know my humble name?
errors.why: 呼喚 means to call out the name, not to know it; the question is about why he shouted it, so the rendering slightly shifts the point.

items.text: 見我管待客人在此喫酒，你便與他三五升米便了，何須直來問我！」
items.answer: Seeing that I am treating guests here with wine, you may simply give him three or five sheng of rice; why must you come to ask me directly!"

items.text: 鲁镇的酒店的格局，是和别处不同的：都是当街一个曲尺形的大柜台，柜里面豫备着热水，可以随时温酒。
items.answer: The layout of the tavern in Lu Town differs from that elsewhere: there is a large counter shaped like a carpenter's square right on the street, and inside the counter hot water is kept ready so that wine can be warmed at any time.

errors.evidence: a large counter shaped like a carpenter's square right on the street
errors.why: 当街 means facing the street, and "right on the street" could suggest the counter sits outdoors; also "the tavern" is singular, whereas 酒店 refers to all taverns in Lu Town.

items.text: 到了年关，掌柜取下粉板说：『孔乙己还欠十九个钱呢！』
items.answer: As the New Year approached, the shopkeeper took down the blackboard and said, "Kong Yiji still owes nineteen qian!"

errors.evidence: nineteen qian!
errors.why: Leaving the currency unit as untranslated pinyin 'qian' without a gloss is opaque to an English reader; 'coins' or 'cash' would be clearer.

errors.evidence: took down the blackboard
errors.why: The 粉板 is a lime-coated board for chalking up debts, so 'blackboard' is slightly inaccurate, though the function is conveyed.

items.text: 孔乙己便涨红了脸，额上的青筋条条绽出，争辩道：『窃书不能算偸……窃书！……读书人的事，能算偸么？』
items.answer: Kong Yiji turned red in the face, with the veins on his forehead bulging as he argued, "Stealing books cannot be called stealing... Stealing books! ... Matters of a scholar can they be called stealing?"

errors.evidence: "Stealing books cannot be called stealing... Stealing books!"
errors.why: The contrast between the refined 窃 and the plain 偸 is lost, because both are rendered as "stealing", which makes the argument read as a contradiction.

errors.evidence: Matters of a scholar can they be called stealing?
errors.why: The question is awkward and ungrammatical English, as it lacks proper inversion or punctuation.

items.text: 又好笑，又不耐烦，懒懒的答他道：『谁要你教，不是草头底下一个来回的回字么？』
items.answer: It was both amusing and irritable; she replied listlessly, "Who needs your teaching? Isn't it simply a 'hui' character with a grass radical on top?"

errors.evidence: she replied listlessly
errors.why: The narrator is the young waiter, 'I' (male); the candidate wrongly makes the speaker 'she' and detaches it from the first-person narrator.

errors.evidence: It was both amusing and irritable
errors.why: This turns the narrator's own feelings into an impersonal statement, and 'irritable' misrenders 不耐烦 (impatient).

errors.evidence: a 'hui' character with a grass radical on top
errors.why: It drops the 来回 (come and go) gloss, which is how the narrator spells out the 回 component of 茴.

items.text: 我的父亲允许了；我也很高兴，因为我早听到闰土这名字，而且知道他和我仿佛年纪，闰月生的，五行缺土，所以他的父亲叫他闰土。
items.answer: My father gave his consent; I was also very happy, for I had long heard the name Runtu and knew that he was of my own age, born in a leap month, lacking earth among the five elements, so his father named him Runtu.

errors.evidence: he was of my own age
errors.why: 仿佛 means roughly or about the same age, not exactly the same.

items.text: 现在我所谓希望，不也是我自己手制的偶像么？
items.answer: Is not the hope I speak of now also an idol made by my own hands?

items.text: 我看出他话中全是毒，笑中全是刀，他们的牙齿，全是白厉厉的排着，这就是吃人的家伙。
items.answer: I saw that his words were all poison, his smile was all knives, and their teeth were lined up menacingly white—these were the men who eat people.

errors.evidence: lined up menacingly white
errors.why: 白厉厉 means gleaming white and sharp or fierce; 'menacingly white' loses the sharp sense of the teeth.

errors.evidence: these were the men who eat people
errors.why: 家伙 also carries an instrument sense, which is lost; the rendering is also past tense for a present, certain statement.

items.text: 我也不怕；虽然不吃人，胆子却比他们还壮。
items.answer: I am not afraid; even though I do not eat people, my courage is greater than theirs.

errors.evidence: I am not afraid;
errors.why: The 也 ('also/for my part') is dropped, losing a slight link to his earlier calm.

errors.evidence: even though I do not eat people, my courage is greater than theirs
errors.why: 'Even though' and the plain comparative miss the concessive 虽然...却 and the intensifying 还 ('even bolder'); 'although ... even bolder' is more natural.

items.text: 子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？人不知而不慍，不亦君子乎？」
items.answer: The Master said, "Is it not delightful to study and then review it from time to time? Is it not joyful when friends come from afar? Is it not the mark of a gentleman to be free of resentment when others do not know him?"

errors.evidence: to study and then review it from time to time
errors.why: "From time to time" slightly blurs 時 (at due times, regularly) toward "occasionally", and "review" narrows 習, though the meaning is largely intact.

items.text: 子曰：「巧言令色，鮮矣仁。」
items.answer: The Master said: "He who is glib in his speech and wears an ingratiating expression has little of benevolence."

items.text: 子曰：「君子食無求飽，居無求安，敏於事而愼於言，就有道而正焉：可謂好學也已。」
items.answer: The Master said: "A gentleman does not seek to be well-fed in his eating, nor to be comfortable in his dwelling; he is diligent in his work and cautious in his speech, and seeks out those who are virtuous to correct himself. This may be called true love of learning."

items.text: 子貢曰：「貧而無諂，富而無驕，何如？」子曰：「可也。未若貧而樂，富而好禮者也」。
items.answer: Zi Gong said, "Is it good to be poor without being obsequious and rich without being arrogant?" The Master replied, "That is acceptable. But it is not as good as being poor yet happy and rich yet fond of ritual."

items.text:
牀前明月光，疑是地上霜。
舉頭望明月，低頭思故鄉。
items.answer: Before my bed the bright moon's light gleams, I wonder if it is frost on the ground. I raise my head to gaze at the bright moon; I lower my head and think of my native land.

items.text:
紅豆生南國，春來發幾枝。
願君多采擷，此物最相思。
items.answer: Red beans grow in the southern land; how many branches bloom when spring comes? I wish you would gather them more, for this is the thing that most stirs thoughts of longing.

errors.evidence: how many branches bloom when spring comes
errors.why: 發 means sprout or put forth shoots, not bloom; this is a slight inaccuracy that leaves the meaning intact.

errors.evidence: I wish you would gather them more
errors.why: 'gather them more' is awkward; 'gather plenty' or 'gather many' is the natural English.

items.text:
千山鳥飛絕，萬徑人蹤滅。
孤舟簑笠翁，獨釣寒江雪。
items.answer: Birds fly from the peaks of Qianshan, and footprints vanish from every path. A lone boatman in a straw raincoat and hat casts his line alone into the cold river's snow.

errors.evidence: Birds fly from the peaks of Qianshan
errors.why: 千山 means 'a thousand mountains' (all the mountains), not a place name 'Qianshan'.

errors.evidence: Birds fly from the peaks
errors.why: 鳥飛絕 means birds have ceased flying; the candidate states that birds fly, which loses the stillness and reverses the meaning.

errors.evidence: footprints vanish from every path
errors.why: This is acceptable for the hyperbole, but it is tense-confused and the first line's meaning is already lost.

errors.evidence: A lone boatman
errors.why: The old man (翁) is rendered as 'boatman', so his age is lost.
